subject: test(attn): cover native FlashAttention replay determinism

requirement.behavior: Retain native FlashAttention numerical-reference and bitwise replay coverage for model-shaped BF16 dense prefill, paged prefill and single-token paged decode. Replay identical inputs after unrelated same-shaped attention work and live allocator churn, rejecting fallback rather than allowing a reference fallback to mask a native regression.
requirement.workload: Intel XPU native FA2; head dimension256,24 query heads,4 KV heads,page size64. Dense prefill lengths104,107,162; paged prefill162; decode query length1 and KV length162. These protect the KVarN first-chunk FA2 helper and ordinary BF16 control paths, not the custom quantized KVarN decode operator itself.
requirement.test_contract: Five parameterized cases, each with a finite-output CPU FP32 attention reference (rtol0.01,atol0.02) and eight exact BF16-bit replay comparisons. Each repeat interleaves a decoy call and a live irregularly sized allocation, then clears the XPU caching allocator.
requirement.final_stack_effect: Test-only delta. The sole affected file has blob46abaa4294185b050b2af831b370190db9d2db55 both at this commit and final fork tip; no subsequent repair, revert or overlap changes it.
requirement.performance_claim: None. These checks establish neither service-wide deterministic text generation nor a speed improvement. Removing this commit changes no serving implementation but loses the replay regression coverage.

upstream_coverage.evidence: The selected unchanged upstream base has broad dense/paged/decode numerical comparisons and sink/window regression checks. The local test reuses the existing independent reference helper instead of copying an oracle. Upstream has no equivalent test_flash_attn_determinism.py or combined native-only, exact model-head, eight-replay, interleaved-decoy and allocator-pressure contract.
upstream_coverage.coverage: Partial numerical coverage; no replacement for the retained replay assertions. No old-to-selected upstream kernel change exists because the exact dependency remains0.1.15.4.

upstream_coverage.evidence: Newer0.1.17 adds graph-mode comparisons, changing ragged/padded speculative metadata, graph-vs-eager sink equality, and head-size72/80 accuracy. Those cover different shape/dispatch/failure contracts. Ragged graph replay checks numerical closeness and inactive-row zeros while inputs/metadata change; it does not test eight bitwise identical eager replays with same-shaped decoys and allocator churn. Sink graph equality is exact but is a different sink/window case. New attention optimizations therefore do not supersede this test-only delta even on the unselected newer base.
upstream_coverage.coverage: Useful complementary upstream tests, not semantic duplication.

upstream_coverage.evidence: v0.33's XPU fa_utils route still obtains flash_attn_varlen_func from xpu_ops. Ordinary FlashAttention remains a consumer, and our KVarN first-chunk/materialized dense helper also calls this interface. The new multimodal-prefix composite and adaptive-verification work do not remove these native paths or make the replay requirement obsolete.
upstream_coverage.coverage: Retained call-path relevance; tests remain independent of the vLLM commit replay.

minimum_residual: Retain the existing223-line test file unchanged as a separate test-only commit. No serving source, schema, package dependency or native operator change is justified by this audit.

dependencies.description: Uses tests.flash_attn.test_flash_attn_varlen_func.ref_paged_attn and vllm_xpu_kernels.flash_attn_interface.flash_attn_varlen_func; the reference helper and fallback hook exist at both inspected kernel bases. No dependency on another local kernel fix or custom KVarN schema is required.

Qualification must compile the BF16 H256 dense causal and paged attention variants plus the Q24/KV4 decode shape. The autouse fallback rejection intentionally fails missing-variant builds instead of claiming native coverage. Brutus's existing host kernel overrides include H256 causal dense/paged and qgroup8,H256,page64 decode variants.
